evidence: Defining behaviour is graded heavily and server-proven: the constraints gate (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:18-24, hro_gate_shared) requires a job+candidate created by a Recruiter to be found by the Observer in a NEW independent browser context and explicitly rejects 'a static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save'; functional repeats this as the global browser gate (scored/functional/prompt.md:11-13). Core pipeline/conversation behaviour has many criteria with independent-context readback by another account (hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder, hro_bulk_move, hro_undo_restores read by Mei Lin; hro_msg_exchange Rafael<->Tomas; hro_stale_refused cross-user conflict; hro_live_board; hro_unread_counts per person). Since another account in another context sees the data, it must be server-backed (not merely same-origin storage). Durability across process restart: hro_restart (functional/judge.toml:410-417, weight 1.5) requires restart_app then fresh sign-in with jobs, card order per stage, notes, messages, unread counts, activity lines and the seeded Platform Engineer order/note unchanged and starting data not reloaded; protocol D (prompt.md:51) makes a restart_app error score 0 and says 'A reload is not a restart'. test.sh:97-111 and 127-193 relaunch the same entry with the same DB_PATH, so the restart genuinely tests on-disk persistence. Reload/re-auth of per-person drafts (instruction.md:7; hireops_rules.md:168-175): hro_drafts (functional:374-381) covers switching conversation/Board and reload; hro_pol_session_resume (polish/judge.toml:52-59, weight 2.5) covers ended session -> sign-in prompt, same person resumes and sends, Mei Lin signing in on the same browser sees neither draft, Rafael's drafts survive. Broken apps tried: (1) in-memory server state -> passes gate but fails hro_restart; (2) localStorage-only board -> fails gate (Observer independent context); (3) reseed-on-start -> fails hro_restart ('not loaded again', review records lost); (4) drafts cleared at sign-out or shared across users on one browser -> fails hro_pol_session_resume. Conforming alternatives tried: server-side drafts (allowed, 'Where drafts are kept is yours') pass the polish row since Mei is a different user; sessions lost on restart are tolerated (hro_restart demands a fresh sign-in). Golden: db.js:9-21,57-84 stores in SQLite at DB_PATH and seeds only when empty. Scripted golden run (workspace.json, hashes verified) reports passed groups 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages, unread counts and activity without reseeding; live updates resume' and 'session ended mid-draft: sign-in prompt, nothing sent, same person resumes and sends; another person sees no draft'. Risk=true only because no full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'): whether the judge reaches protocol D and successfully calls restart_app within the 9000 s functional budget after the long protocol sequence is unmeasured; if budget is exhausted, hro_restart becomes NOT EXERCISED and durability would be unproven in practice. Minor observation (not a defect): restart durability carries 1.5 of 59.5 functional weight, so an in-memory server loses little; weighting is the concern of other rows.
